newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to finish Gdanski sell-off in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Poland to finish Gdanski sell-off in 1997.

text.p: The Polish Finance Ministry wants to complete the privatisation of Bank Gdanski SA next year in a public tender of treasury shares but has yet to set the date of the offering, a senior ministry official said on Friday.
"We want to take steps which will allow us to complete the Bank Gdanski privatisation next year," Wieslaw Federowicz, the head of the ministry's banking department, told Reuters.
"Bank Gdanski shares will be sold through a public tender but so far we don't have a specific method ready. I think it will take a few months," he said.

Earlier on Friday HSBC Investment Bank, which managed Gdanski's Global Depositary Receipts (GDR) issue in December 1995, freed the treasury from a lockup agreement which prevented it from selling its shares before December 18.

The treasury now holds 39.9 percent of Bank Gdanski and plans to retain only five percent. International investors have subscribed to about 20 percent of Gdanski in the form of GDRs and Poland's Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA (BIG) holds about 30 percent of shares.
Federowicz said the treasury sought to be freed from the lockup ahead of the deadline because it wanted to start preparing for the sale early on.

"We have applied for HSBC's consent because we did not want to wait until December 18, as the Finance Ministry agreed not only to hold onto shares until that date but also to refrain from any actions leading to the sale," he said.
